FrozenLake-v1.name: FrozenLake (Slippery)
FrozenLake-v1.description: Navigate a frozen lake from start to goal without falling into holes. The surface is slippery, making movement stochastic.

sections.goal: Reach the goal tile (G) starting from the start tile (S) without falling into holes (H).

stateSpace.description: 16 tiles in a 4×4 grid. Each tile represents one state.

rewards.description: Sparse reward: +1 for reaching goal, 0 otherwise.

sections.stochasticity: Slippery surface: 33% chance of moving perpendicular to intended direction.
sections.difficulty: The 4×4 version has ~0.7 optimal success rate due to stochasticity.

FrozenLake-v1-NoSlip.name: FrozenLake (No Slip)
FrozenLake-v1-NoSlip.description: Navigate a frozen lake from start to goal without falling into holes. The surface is NOT slippery, making movement deterministic.

sections.goal: Reach the goal tile (G) starting from the start tile (S) without falling into holes (H).

stateSpace.description: 16 tiles in a 4×4 grid. Each tile represents one state.

rewards.description: Sparse reward: +1 for reaching goal, 0 otherwise.

sections.stochasticity: Deterministic: Agent always moves in the intended direction.
sections.difficulty: Easier than slippery version. Optimal policy achieves 100% success rate.

CartPole-v1.name: CartPole
CartPole-v1.description: Balance a pole upright on a moving cart by pushing the cart left or right. The classic first environment for deep reinforcement learning.

sections.goal: Keep the pole balanced upright as long as possible. The episode ends when the pole tips more than 12° from vertical, the cart moves more than 2.4 units from the center, or 500 steps are reached (success).

stateSpace.description: Four continuous values: cart position, cart velocity, pole angle, pole angular velocity. Because the state is continuous, a Q-table is impossible - this is why a neural network (DQN) is needed.

rewards.description: +1 for every timestep the pole stays up - so the episode return equals the episode length, and the reward chart directly shows how long the agent balances.

sections.stochasticity: Deterministic dynamics; only the initial state is slightly randomized.
sections.difficulty: Considered solved at an average return of 475+ over 100 episodes (max 500).

MountainCar-v0.name: MountainCar
MountainCar-v0.description: Drive an underpowered car out of a valley. The engine is too weak to climb directly - the agent must learn to build momentum by swinging back and forth.

sections.goal: Reach the flag on the right hill. The car's engine cannot climb the slope directly, so the agent must first drive away from the goal to gain momentum - a strategy it has to discover on its own.

stateSpace.description: Two continuous values: the car's position along the track and its velocity. Continuous states rule out a Q-table - a neural network (DQN) is needed.

rewards.description: -1 for every timestep until the flag is reached (episode cap: 200 steps). The return therefore equals minus the episode length - faster solutions score higher, and an agent that never reaches the flag gets -200.

sections.stochasticity: Deterministic dynamics; only the initial position is slightly randomized.
sections.difficulty: Hard exploration: random actions almost never reach the flag, so the agent sees no reward signal for a long time. Considered solved at an average return of -110 or better over 100 episodes. Try PPO here: it will most likely FAIL. PPO is on-policy - it learns only from its own most recent episodes - and since random behavior essentially never reaches the flag, every episode returns exactly -200: all advantages are zero and the policy gradient carries no information at all. DQN escapes this trap with its replay buffer (one lucky success is stored and reused for thousands of updates) and its optimistic initial value estimates; PPO has neither.
